t: Notwithstanding section 1101, section 408 of division E of Public Law 112–74 (125 Stat. 1038) shall be applied to funds appropriated by this division by substituting “112–10, and 112–74” for “112–10” and by substituting “2012” for “2011”.

fable.w: This section is a technical appropriations cross-reference that applies section 408 of division E of Public Law 112-74 to funds in this division by substituting public law numbers and a year. There is no tempting participation reading on its face: it mentions no consultation, hearing, rulemaking, advisory body, or right to sue, and no party outside the federal government. The underlying section 408 is not reproduced here, so nothing in this text itself brings outsiders into a federal decision.

opus.w: This is a technical appropriations provision. It extends an existing section to cover more funds by updating the public law numbers and fiscal year it refers to. No one outside the federal government is consulted, given a hearing or comment period, or given a right to sue. The cross-reference alone is not enough to show participation, because nothing in this text describes an outside-party process.
opus.s: section 408 of division E of Public Law 112–74 (125 Stat. 1038) shall be applied to funds appropriated by this division by substituting “112–10, and 112–74” for “112–10” and by substituting “2012” for “2011”.
opus.b:
1. **Tempting reading:** Someone might think the cross-reference to section 408 of Public Law 112–74 brings in whatever process that section sets up. But the text I have only changes which appropriations laws and fiscal years section 408 applies to. It mentions no outside party, no consultation, hearing, comment period, rulemaking or right to sue, so it fails the definition's test that a non-federal party must be involved in a federal decision.

qwen_chat.w: This section is a technical amendment regarding the application of funds and statutory references. It does not create any advisory bodies, comment periods, hearings, or consultation requirements with outside parties. It involves only internal legislative and executive branch adjustments to appropriation codes and dates.
qwen_chat.s: Notwithstanding section 1101, section 408 of division E of Public Law 112–74 (125 Stat. 1038) shall be applied to funds appropriated by this division by substituting “112–10, and 112–74” for “112–10” and by substituting “2012” for “2011”.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that because the text references other laws (Public Law 112-74), it implicitly involves the processes defined in those laws, which might include participation. However, this specific section is merely a technical amendment to appropriation references and dates. It does not itself establish any mechanism for outside parties to consult, comment, or participate in a decision. It is purely administrative and internal to the legislative/executive funding process.
